_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/aim-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch, so the backbone builds and loads in-process; use an absolute path for --python). This is the A3:aim wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md): AIM reused as a frozen spatial-backbone kind for the ARSSL harness. AIM is hand-written and non-timm, so -- like MAE and I-JEPA -- it ships its own downstream_backbone.py provider, discovered by the shared layer (the shared discovery/dispatch/KINDS guards are already proven in mutations/mae-backbone.json). AIM's forward returns a training tuple, so features come from AIMViT.forward_features(x, layer_ids) -- the last num_feature_layers blocks averaged, patch-mean-pooled -- reshaped to a [B,C,h,w] map. These mutations prove the provider's guards are not vacuous: the right layers are read and reshaped faithfully (pooling the map reproduces AIM's own probe feature), the prediction head's absence is tolerated while a missing trunk weight or an alien key is refused, and the backbone stays frozen in eval.
